findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: OpenCode 2's serve may already bind loopback by default and refuse a non-loopback bind without an explicit flag, making the omitted flag redundant; the repository cannot confirm this and runner network isolation would mask it in CI.
findingDetails.claim: The battery's private server bind address is left to OpenCode 2's default, so the loopback posture its client and port probe assume is unverified.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Searched the file for host pinning: only findFreePort (probe.listen(0,'127.0.0.1')) and the client serverUrl name loopback; the spawn carries no host flag. Diff check shows the spawn is unchanged by the merge. waitForBanner requires a listening line and a password before any request, so pre-auth exposure is limited.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to a note once serve is shown to default to loopback; escalate to P1 if the default binds every interface, since the child then serves the caller's credentials beyond the host boundary.
findingDetails.scopeProof: File is inside the declared review scope; the serve spawn is a context line in git diff 06d02096e90^1 06d02096e90, so the posture is inherited in a reviewed file rather than introduced by the merge.
findingDetails.title: The doctor battery starts its private OpenCode 2 server without pinning the bind address, while handing it the whole parent environment

findingDetails.alternativeExplanation: Ignoring an unsupported key may equal the host ignoring it, and warning on every unmapped key would be noise while the set is small and stable; the counter is that a hard guard degrading to a no-op should fail loudly rather than fail open.
findingDetails.claim: dualPlugin silently ignores hook keys outside MAPPED_HOOKS, so a guard that registers an unmapped key loads without effect and without any failing signal.
findingDetails.counterevidenceSought: Read the whole setup path for a warn or throw on skippedKeys: none. Both shipped guard plugins use tool.execute.before, which is mapped, so the drop is latent. The six-entry set is the bridge's own translation table, so the drop is the bridge's decision.
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade to a note if the registration test family asserts each guard plugin's hook keys are all in MAPPED_HOOKS, or if the host rejects unknown keys before the bridge sees them. Escalate to P1 if a shipped guard plugin registers a key outside the set.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Bridge and plugins are inside the declared review scope; the claim is limited to the mapping table and the drop path, and the guard plugins were read only to establish that their keys are mapped.
findingDetails.title: An unmapped plugin hook key is dropped with no runtime signal, so a guard plugin's block can silently become a no-op on OpenCode 2
